successors.note: The page: 'The Dutch took control in 1819'. The sultans stayed as Dutch dependants (Abu Bakar Tajuddin II was exiled in 1854) until the sultanate 'joined the Republic of the United States of Indonesia (RIS) in 1950', so the Dutch East Indies dossier may want a vassal tint 1819-1950. Cliopatria's Dutch East Indies shape reaches the Sambas coast only from c. 1830.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's Sambas row begins in 1619, the page has the kingdom in 1609 (its infobox says 1600, its sultan list 1675). The page gives no boundary; it describes the early territory as the Sambas River and its tributaries plus the Paloh River, so the outline is generous for these years.

5.8 k km2, from Tanjung Datuk to the Duri River (lat 0.93-2.02 N). The page puts that extent under Abu Bakar Kamal ud-din I (1732-1764) and adds the Selakau River under Muhammad Taj ud-din I (1685-1708), so before about 1700 the true realm was smaller than the outline; the page dates no step, so the outline stands. No infobox area to compare.

ledger.note: 1609: Sambas becomes a kingdom under Sepudak. 'At first governed by governors, Sambas became a kingdom in 1609 with the descendant of Sepudak.' The infobox says 'Established: 1600' and the ruler list opens the Sultanate in 1675; the year here is the text's.

1675: the Panembahan Ratu line becomes the Sultanate under Muhammad Shafi ud-din I, the first Muslim ruler (infobox religion 'Hinduism (until 1675)'). The text says the sultanate was 'first established by Raden Sulaiman' without a year; the ruler list gives 1675. Same state and land: colour continues.

ledger.note: 1819: the Dutch take control of Sambas. 'The Dutch took control in 1819', after the British expeditions of 1812 and 1813 (the second 'captured Sambas'). The sultans survive as Dutch dependants to 1950.

wars.note: The page does not say how long the British held the town or who gave it up; the Dutch 'took control in 1819'. No territory is recorded as changing hands.

notes: One page was opened (budget 1-2). The page gives three founding dates (infobox 1600, text 1609, ruler list 1675); the dossier starts at 1609 (the kingdom) and treats 1675 as the change to a sultanate. The Cliopatria outline is the late extent (Tanjung Datuk to the Duri River, with Montrado, Bengkayang, Seluas and Sungkung under Abu Bakar Kamal ud-din I, and the Selakau River under Muhammad Taj ud-din I): it overstates the early realm but no page dates the steps. Brunei: the page says only that a ruler's daughter married the Brunei prince Tengah (infobox 'Arrival of Sultan Tengah: 1639'), whose son became the first Muslim sultan; no land passed (the sultanate-of-brunei dossier carries a 1619 'loss' of three cells to Sambas, which is Cliopatria's step, not a page's). The dossier ends in 1819 with the Dutch takeover although the sultans reigned on, under Dutch control, to 1950: the Dutch East Indies dossier should tint the land as a dependency 1819-1950 if the project wants it. The Chinese kongsi republics of Monterado and Mandor and the 1836 Sarawak uprising are not on the page. No Sambas place name is in the gazetteer.
